featured_reviews.name: Akshay P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Helluuu guys,

Visited National near Bandra station 2 days ago. If you’re expecting a fancy ambience or modern cafe type setup, this is not that kind of place. But if you want really good North Indian food at a budget price, this place is definitely worth trying.

The setup is very basic with non AC seating and shared wooden benches. Has that old school fast moving Mumbai food spot vibe. The place gets crowded, especially during lunch and dinner time, but service is quick.

One thing I liked is that they still cook food on traditional coal stoves, so you get that smoky flavour in the food which actually makes a difference.

I tried paneer burji along with roti, Mirchi Laccha Paratha and butter naan. Taste was really good overall and all these were suggested by a guy outside who said veg items are famous there. I liked the food, but personally I would suggest trying something other than paneer burji if you want the best experience.

I also heard their Chicken Mughlai and Chicken Liver Masala are really popular among non veg lovers.

Don’t miss their chaach as well. Very refreshing with the food.

Price is honestly one of the best parts. A proper meal for two can be done within around 300 to 500 easily.

Overall, simple place, great taste and very budget friendly.

featured_reviews.name: Rishikesh Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imlee – The Chaat Gali offers a modern twist on traditional Indian street food in the heart of Bandra. The ambiance is chic and inviting, providing a comfortable setting for chaat enthusiasts.  ￼

Food:
The menu showcases a variety of regional chaats, including Pani Puri, Bhel Puri, and Aloo Tikki, each prepared with a contemporary flair. While the use of fresh ingredients is evident, some dishes might benefit from bolder flavors to capture the authentic street food essence.  ￼

Service:
The staff is attentive and ensures a pleasant dining experience. However, during peak hours, service can be slightly delayed due to high demand.

Value for Money:
Considering the upscale ambiance and quality ingredients, the pricing is reasonable. It’s a great spot for those looking to enjoy street food in a more refined environment. ￼

Overall Experience:
Imlee is a commendable attempt to elevate traditional chaats for a modern audience. While there’s room for enhancing the authenticity of flavors, it’s worth a visit for those seeking a unique chaat experience in Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Noel Rodriques
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love street food, Imlee - The Chaat Galli is a must-visit! 🌟
Their Pani Puri cart is magic — imagine tasting Delhi ke Golgappe, Kolkata ke Puchka, and Mumbai ki Pani Puri all at one place! Each one was fresh, crispy, and full of flavour.h

We also tried their Dahi Bhalle and Papdi Chaat — both were loaded with dahi and perfectly balanced masalas. The Cheese Pav Bhaji was rich, creamy, and super satisfying.

And to end on a sweet note — the Meerut ki Jalebi totally stole the show! Crispy, juicy, and just the right amount of sweetness.

The place has a lovely ambiance where you can actually sit and enjoy your street food cravings in comfort. Highly recommend this spot for chaat lovers in the city!

✅ Tip: Don’t miss the Pani Puri cart experience — it’s fun and delicious!

featured_reviews.name: Sneha
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Imlee, Santacruz, we recently tried a few things. We started with three varieties of everyon’s favourite - Panipuri, Golgappa and Puchka. Then we had Dilli ki famous Rani Kachori Chaat which was highly recommended by Curly Tales. Honestly, I had never eaten this inspite of many trips to Delhi.  Then we had Agra ke Matar Poori our Kacche Tamatar ki Sabji.
Kadhi Chawal from Haridwar ki Gali was another staff recommendation. This kinda took me back to the Kadhi chawal from Chotiwala in Rishikesh. Simple and perfect!
We finished our meal with Ras Malai.
There were many more items on the menu. All regional street food from North and Central India. Everything we ate here left us wanting more. The staff’s recommendations were on point. This is Imlee by Neeti Goel & Curly Tales, a cute place where you have your favourite street food under one roof. Check it out.

featured_reviews.name: abhishek nair

We tried pani puri, pav bhaji, puchka, chole bhature, and rani kachori—all were full of authentic flavors. A must-visit for anyone craving delicious Indian street food!

featured_reviews.name: Komal Jaisingh
featured_reviews.review_text:

Their menu brings together iconic flavors from Mathura, Agra, Indore, Rajasthan, Amritsar, Delhi, and Mumbai—each dish felt like a little journey across India.
From spicy pani puri to rich paneer chole bhature and the dreamy Jodhpuri gulab jamun, every bite was full of authentic, homely goodness.
A must-visit if you're craving soulful, desi comfort food with a regional twist!

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Upadhyay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imlee Chaat Gali in Santacruz West is a total flavour bomb! If you’re someone who lives for street-style food but also loves a great vibe and ambience, this place is going to win your heart.

Every dish I tried was lipsmacking and delicious—from the tangy chaats to spicy snacks, the flavors are just spot-on. It’s like the best of Indian streets served up in a trendy, clean, and super fun setting. 😋✨

What really stood out? The ambience. It’s not just a restaurant, it’s an experience. Think colorful, energetic, and full of character—perfect for catching up with friends, clicking some aesthetic pics, or simply enjoying great food with a side of great vibes.

This place nails the balance between authentic street food charm and modern restaurant comfort. Will 100% be back to explore more from their menu!

featured_reviews.name: juhi roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of Indian street food but want to enjoy it in a clean, comfy setting with lovely vibes — Imlee by Chaat gali  is a must-visit!

I went with my family and absolutely loved the experience. From the fun twist of three flavours of Panipuri to the comforting Jodhpur pyaaz kachori, everything was full of flavour and nostalgia.

We also tried the Amritsari chole bhature, Rani Kachori Chaat, and the super refreshing Vrindavan-style lassi served in kulhad — all spot on. And the Meerut-style jalebi with rabdi? Ended the meal on such a sweet note!

The ambiance is beautiful and staff is really warm — perfect for a family outing or a chill meal with friends. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Bhumika Shanbhag

This can officially be termed as a total chaat-lover's paradise! The place has a vibrant vibe, and the food just hits the chatpata spot.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Great Korean Street-Food Experience in Khar West!
If you’re around Bandra/Khar and looking to try Korean cuisine, Seoul Dak is a must-visit spot. It’s a popular Korean street-food-style restaurant known for bringing authentic Korean flavours into a casual, fun setting. The brand focuses on classic Korean comfort foods like K-style fried chicken (their signature), Korean corn dogs, ramen, bao, tteokbokki, kimchi dumplings and more — many inspired by the street food scene in Seoul.  ￼

🍽️ What we tried:
Drinks:
• Matcha Bubble Tea
• Taro Bubble Tea

Starters & Mains:
• Cheese Pull Bao
• Cheese Corn Dog
• Egg & Cheese Soupy Ramen
• Ganjang Boneless Bite Chicken
• K-BBQ Korean Fried Chicken
• Kimchi King Dumpling
• Kimchi Fries

Dessert:
• Strawberry Bingsu

Everything tasted great — from the crispy Korean fried chicken to the flavorful, cheesy bites and refreshing bingsu. The bubble teas were smooth and a nice cool complement to the food.

👍 Service & Ambience:
Management and service were friendly and attentive. The vibe is casual and vibrant — perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or a date spot if you’re craving Korean flavours.

📍 What it’s known for:
Seoul Dak is one of the first Korean QSR-style concepts in India focused on street food classics with authentic touch points developed with Korean recipes, including their standout fried chicken and other staples like corn dogs and ramen.  ￼

✅ Would recommend: Definitely add this to your list if you’re in Bandra/Khar West and want bold, Korean-inspired eats with a fun, quick-serve vibe.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Bandstand Pantry is one of those cafés that remains popular for good reason. Located right by Bandstand, it works especially well for a relaxed breakfast, a solo meal, or an easy outing with family.

The menu has enough variety to suit different moods and appetites — from smoothies, smoothie bowls, sandwiches, and salads to more comforting options like mac and cheese and mushroom pâté. They also have a good selection of egg dishes and teas & coffees (hot or cold). My kids especially enjoy the mac and cheese, the chicken mushroom pâté, and the hot chocolate, while I keep going back for the lemon mint iced tea. Their avocado-on-toast options are also worth mentioning, especially because they offer a smaller portion size — something I genuinely appreciate when dining alone.

Because the café has open seating on the main road, evenings can get noisy. Breakfast, however, is a very different experience — calmer, with a sea view and the sound of the waves in the background. The strong fans and sea breeze also make the outdoor seating more comfortable than you might expect.

What stands out most to me is the attention to hygiene and service. Tables are cleared and cleaned quickly, and the staff is alert and efficient. I have also noticed them actively keeping crows away in the mornings so guests can eat in peace — a small but very real detail in this location.

A special mention for the staff member who usually greets guests at the entrance. He is warm, quick to help with seating, and knows the menu well enough to make thoughtful recommendations.

For a meal for two, the pricing feels reasonable for the area. It is also pet-friendly, which adds to its appeal. Overall, Bandstand Pantry is a dependable option when you want a comfortable café meal in Bandra, especially if you are looking for something that works well before or after a walk or workout at Bandstand.

featured_reviews.name: Arshad Mir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Brunched at MAG St. Bandra recently and as someone who’s eaten through enough of Bombay’s brunch circuit to know when a place is pure hype versus when there’s actual substance behind the aesthetic — MAG St definitely falls in the latter category. The food is genuinely good. The problem? They’ve started pricing like they’re in Notting Hill or Le Marais.

Started strong with the watermelon feta salad — fresh, balanced and properly refreshing, though ice-cold watermelon would’ve taken it up another notch in Bombay heat. The dim sums were fair play overall. The truffle edamame dumplings were decent but forgettable, while the shrimp in ginger broth dumplings were the clear standout. That broth/sauce situation was excellent.

The Asian fried rice was honestly a surprise hit. Comforting, flavourful, generous enough portion-wise — though realistically this is a ₹550 dish masquerading as an ₹825 one because Bandra brunch economics require everything to sound “premium” enough for the Bandra aunties and influencer crowd.

Then came the smoked salmon eggs benedict — the dish everyone seems to post here. It was alright. Not bad by any means, but I’ve definitely had better at Sarabeth's. The hollandaise was absolutely drenched over the eggs to the point it overpowered everything else a bit.

The real stars? The drinks. Phenomenal. Especially the Summer Thirst — probably the best thing we ordered all afternoon.

Bill came to around ₹5.4k for two (roughly £42 / €49), which honestly could and probably should have landed closer to ₹4k. But then again, this is Bandra in 2026 — people here are happily paying London and Paris brunch prices while sitting off Linking Road, so fair play to MAG St for understanding their market perfectly.

Overall: stylish spot, genuinely solid kitchen, not just Instagram fluff — but you’re definitely paying a Bandra premium on top of the food.

The vibe is warm and inviting with a great ambience. The staff were attentive, friendly and helpful throughout

Parking in the Bandra can be challenging, so plan a bit of extra time if you’re driving in.

Priced on the higher side ₹2,700 for two, which feels fair for the quality and portions

Coming back definitely to explore more from the menu!

featured_reviews.review_text: I wanted to visit this place long time a go just because of concept found it interesting. featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a Must try when in Mumbai, Their speciality Herb Chicken Pav & Mutton Shammi Pav is a Hot seller, There is also Vegetarian Options for Veg lovers. Highly recommend this place, U will keep coming back once you have it.

featured_reviews.review_text: Great place to pick up a quick, filling and satisfying snack. Love the fact that they serve Old school fruits with each pav. featured_reviews.name: Bangkokian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great dining experience at Ferry Wharf Seafood Restaurant – Bandra Reclamation (West) and really enjoyed every dish. 🦀🦞

The seafood was very fresh, and it was nice to see the selection before cooking. We tried several dishes, and everything was delicious, well cooked, and full of flavor. The crab, prawns, and fish were especially good fresh, tender, and perfectly seasoned.

Being a vegetarian, I ordered Cream Brocolli, Cheese Stuffed Potatoes as starters and dal and rice for mains. I would like to recommend the Brocolli starter and the cheese naan is to die for!

My non-vegetarian company tried prawns fish thali, rava fish fry and chicken kebabs along with some other dishes. But everything in non-veg section was amazing. The staff also let us pick up a crab for pictures.

The staff paid attention to our needs and were very good hosts! Loved my experience. Won't mind visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Rahil Kotadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is conveniently located near Lilavati Hospital and Wings Sports Club. From the outside, it looks appealing — well-lit and nicely decorated — but the experience changes once you step in. The seating is uncomfortable, and the tables were not properly cleaned. The person at the counter, who seems to be handling both orders and service, appeared disinterested and unwelcoming. Instead of attending to customers, he was often occupied with his phone, which made the overall atmosphere even less inviting.

We ordered idly to begin with, but it was hard and tasted stale. The chutneys had good flavour and texture, but they were clearly served straight from the freezer. The sambhar didn’t resemble sambhar at all — it had an odd and unpleasant taste. The filter coffee was another letdown, made with regular Nescafé instant coffee, with nothing “filter” about it.

What was most disappointing was the service approach. We were three people and received only one disposable spoon. When we requested an additional spoon, the server reluctantly gave us one and then added ₹5 to the bill without informing us and without any mention of such charges anywhere.

Overall, this place was an utter disappointment, both in terms of food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Dipasha Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text: Superb!! So so so underrated and underhyped. Each and everything we are absolutely delicious. Thatte idli, benne ragi dosa, payasam, pineapple sheera and filter coffee must try. So warm and yum. Ambience also good. Rates are reasonable according to location. Much better compared to benne dosa, no waiting time here and seating also available.

featured_reviews.name: Gautam Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text: A small place with 3 tables and one table with tall stools - can seat at most 15 persons. The podi, sambhar and rassam tastes were not up to the mark - too spicy, too much garlic and tasted unlike the normal podi, sambhar and rassam. Had to skip drinking the rassam. The Benne Dosa was however very good. The Benne Rava Dosa was okay - thin and crisp. The masala filling was also okay. No valet parking - one has to find parking nearby.

featured_reviews.name: Fatty Lakdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're craving truly authentic South Indian food, this place is a hidden gem! The Thatte Idli here is soft, fluffy, and melts in your mouth — perfectly complemented by their flavorful chutneys and piping hot sambar.

The Benne Dosa is another must-try — golden, crisp on the outside, and rich with buttery goodness. Every bite feels indulgent yet comfortingly traditional.

What truly stands out is the value for money. Generous portions, quality ingredients, and pocket-friendly pricing make it a place you'd want to keep coming back to.

Whether you're a fan of South Indian cuisine or just discovering it, this restaurant is a delightful experience that won’t disappoint. Highly recommended!

I would like to share my experience from my visit today. I went to the stall around 3:50 PM and asked for a coffee. The lady at the counter seemed upset and was not very welcoming. When I asked about the coffee, she informed me that it would take time as the shift was changing and said it was not possible to serve immediately.

When I asked how long it would take, I was told around 30 minutes. I was surprised that a simple shift change would require such a long waiting time.

After about 10 minutes, the new staff arrived, and I again asked if I could get tea or coffee. I received the same response. The staff informed me from a distance that it would take time, without making much effort to assist.

The main concern is the hospitality and customer service. At an airport, where customers often have limited time, this kind of attitude creates a poor experience. Please improve the service approach and ensure customers are treated with more care and professionalism.

Some of us went for the vegetarian options, and even those who usually prefer non-veg were impressed by how tasty and satisfying the veg dishes were. The drinks were another highlight! Each one had a unique twist — refreshing, creative, and beautifully presented. They went so well with the food and really added to the whole dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. featured_reviews.review_text:
Had lunch at The Village Shop today with my husband and overall it was a good experience. The food was fresh, wholesome, and it’s definitely a great place for people with allergies, dietary restrictions, or specific food preferences.

There was one mix-up where potato was added instead of sweet potato mash in one of the dishes, but the team replaced it with exotic vegetables without any issue, which we appreciated.

The only area that could really improve is the service and ingredient awareness among the staff. Our waiter didn’t seem very well informed about the ingredients and communication could have been better, especially for a place that caters to special diets and allergies. He was also taking the order from behind the counter instead of coming to the table, which felt a little impersonal.

That said, it’s still a lovely place with great potential, and this feedback is only to help make the experience even better with more informed and attentive staff.

featured_reviews.name: Neeraja Sundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very ghastly and amusing experience at the Village Shop. I spent a Monday morning here, was hoping to get my coffee and breakfast  in some peace and quiet. It was only me in the cafe and the owner with 2 of her staff on another table.
In the first 10 mins I figured the owner had issues with staff, even though they spoke in hushed tones.

I let it slide. Naturally, I have no context of that conversation.
The food wasn’t up to the mark. They had it replaced without getting defensive.

Then, after a few mins I spoke loudly because I was on a call, and there was no one else in the cafe but me and the owner, I was asked to speak softly. She was irked. I gladly obliged.

I stepped outside to take my call. For 45 mins. In the heat. You see, I have been brought up with a lot of empathy.
It felt like my grandmother gave me a punishment to not enter the house.

What a ghastly experience for a Bandra cafe.  I hope the owners have the business acumen to start something else of their own. Customer centricity and empathy are not the strongest suit of some of the most affluent people in Bandra. What tarnishes reputation is lack of empathy for staff and no understanding of what customer focus looks like.

Money can’t buy you manners or class.

Its evident to me today, yet again :)

featured_reviews.name: Aaliyah Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Frisbee in Bandra, and here’s the honest take… it’s small, crowded, slightly chaotic… but the food makes it worth it.
We began with their super spicy chicken strips, and when I say spicy, I mean fire-level heat. Crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and unapologetically bold, definitely not for the faint-hearted.
Next came the mini sliders, which I absolutely loved. The chicken was tender, flavorful, and perfectly balanced within those soft buns. Bite-sized, but packed with taste.
The real highlight, though, was the Nashville chicken burger. I’ve tried Nashville style chicken at many places, but this one was on a completely different level. The spice, the crunch, the juiciness, everything just worked. Easily one of the best I’ve had. And their fries deserve credit too, golden, crisp, and addictive.
The drinks were fairly average, your standard mojitos and regular options. Nothing bad, just nothing extraordinary.

The only downside? Space. It’s a very small outlet, and you often end up waiting outside for an hour or more. Inside, it can feel quite congested. But once you get your food, the wait starts making sense.

featured_reviews.review_text:
As someone raised in the Middle East, I can confidently say this is an authentic Persian food spot and I can’t wait to go back!

We visited to celebrate my dad’s birthday, and right at the start, I asked Mr. Arwaz from their staff if they could add a “Happy Birthday” message when we ordered dessert. He warmly agreed, and that set the tone for a lovely evening.

We began with two drinks: Dough (their yoghurt-soda version of Masala Chaas) and the Tokyo e Sharbati (saffron, rose water, basil seeds), I especially loved the second one! The hummus was smooth, fresh, and paired beautifully with the flaky Barbari bread.

For mains, we ordered the recommended Persian Platter. Each item had distinct, yummy flavors, but the Lamb Koobideh was the star reminding me of my growing-up days. That's what I will order separately the next time I visit.

We also had the Saffron rice with Ghormeh Sabzi (lamb + beans), which was wonderfully hearty. What stood out was how flavorful everything was without relying on too much spice.

Though I was too full to order dessert, the staff surprised us with a complimentary chocolate tart topped with a “Happy Birthday” note. Such a thoughtful and sweet gesture!

To finish, we were served complimentary black tea with just the right touch of cardamom. Overall, amazing food, warm hospitality, and a truly memorable experience. Highly recommended!
